sanskrit_verse:
कथं चन न कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः कर्म वार्षलम् ।
वृषलः कर्म न ब्राह्मं पतनीये हि ते तयोः ॥
transliteration: kathaṃ cana na kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ karma vārṣalam | vṛṣalaḥ karma na brāhmaṃ patanīye hi te tayoḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: A Brāhmaṇa must never perform actions designated for the Vṛṣala; likewise, a Vṛṣala must never perform actions designated for the Brāhmaṇa—both are liable to fall from their respective dharmic stations.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from inherent capacity, not external designation
Causation arises from alignment with svadharma, not social convention
Capacity-based responsibility is immutable and consciousness-rooted
Restoration logic requires return to one's intrinsic dharma
executable_legal_axioms: IF actor performs action outside assigned svadharma THEN actor incurs liability to fall from station
IF actor assumes role beyond innate capacity THEN system must initiate restoration protocol
IF societal role conflicts with svadharma THEN realign through consciousness-based reintegration
IF individual performs unauthorized karma THEN restore original dharma position without punitive measure
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that no person may assume functions beyond their innate capacity or constitutional station. Violation results in automatic loss of legitimacy and necessitates restorative intervention rather than punitive sanction.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that misalignment with svadharma causes natural fallacy; anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential deviation from truth-consciousness; proportional responsibility lies in returning to source-dharma; non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering is not justice but distortion.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Svadharma Realignment Process to restore proper function
Engage Consciousness Reconnection Protocol to reaffirm innate capacity
Implement Integrity Restoration Sequence to eliminate false-role identification
Execute Dharma Station Completion Ritual to reinstate rightful place
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Dharma is restored when each being aligns with its svadharma; reality responds only to truth, not punishment; consciousness alone adjudicates rightly.
